author: Grand Canyon Times
title: Independent oversight of Arizona corrections system proposed in new legislation
text:
Walt Blackman Arizona Representative | Wikipedia
Walt Blackman Arizona Representative | Wikipedia
Arizona State Representative Walt Blackman has expressed his support for SB1507, a bill proposed by Senator Shawnna Bolick aimed at establishing independent oversight of Arizona's corrections system. Blackman, who chairs the House Government Committee, highlighted the state's significant expenditure on its prison system, amounting to nearly $1.8 billion annually. He emphasized the need for independent oversight to ensure responsible spending and safe housing for inmates.
"Arizona spends nearly $1.8 billion a year on its prison system—the second-largest item in our state budget," Blackman said. "To make sure that money is spent wisely and that inmates are housed safely and responsibly, we need more than selective updates and closed-door briefings from ADCRR. We need independent oversight backed by facts."
SB1507 proposes creating an office with the authority to investigate complaints, inspect facilities, and report publicly. Blackman described this as a necessary accountability measure, contrasting it with the current reliance on whistleblower tips and limited information.
"The bill provides the oversight structure we need to identify problems early, improve conditions, and avoid expensive failures," he added. "It doesn’t replace internal oversight—it adds what’s been missing."
Blackman also noted that both Director Thornell and ADCRR could benefit from this initiative alongside Arizona taxpayers. The bill passed unanimously in the House Government Committee, where Blackman voiced his pride in supporting it.
"I urge my colleagues to pass it on the House floor," he concluded. "Oversight drives accountability—and accountability delivers better outcomes."
Representative Walt Blackman serves Legislative District 7 as a Republican member of the Arizona House of Representatives.
